name: 07_supplier_identity_resync
description: Stage 0 template matching identifies this document via keyword-fingerprint similarity to a DIFFERENT supplier's saved template (near-duplicate layouts/fingerprints are common — see CLAUDE.md/processing.log notes on templates 10-13 being created from garbled OCR text with near-identical phashes). That template's own stored anchor ('Remit To' -> right) lands on a payment-processor name printed on this document, seeding a provisional supplier_name of 'Acme Corp Holdings' at 85% (template_anchor). Stage 2 then applies this supplier's OWN previously-taught anchor ('Supplier' -> right, usage_count 4, learned confidence 1.0 -> 95%), which reads the document's real vendor line and produces 'Greenfield Logistics Ltd' — a different value, at higher confidence, in results['supplier_name']. Pre-fix, engine.py's local `supplier_name` variable stayed frozen at the Stage-0 template guess ('Acme Corp Holdings') for every downstream lookup/persistence (_supplier_name, hint/anchor/logo writes), even though the field the user sees and confirms already reads 'Greenfield Logistics Ltd' — silently teaching the learning corpus the wrong identity on every confirm. This fixture pins the fix: the final `_supplier_name` (and the persisted identity derived from it) must track the LATER, anchor-derived value in results['supplier_name'], not the earlier template guess.
represents: The general supplier-identity-drift CLASS at the Stage 0 -> Stage 2 boundary — any time an early-stage provisional supplier guess (template match, logo match, hint text-scan) is subsequently superseded by a higher-confidence later-stage read of the actual page (keyword, anchor, anchor_crop). Will recur for any future supplier whose template/logo collides with another's, unless the pipeline always re-resolves its 'who is this' from the latest, most-reliable field value rather than freezing it at first guess.
